Purpose and exclusions

A small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Author DA_Dungeon_SluiceVault with entrance/exit IDs, four-member limit, checkpoint and boss definitions. Create L_SluiceVault as a graybox interior with navigation and camera-occlusion tests.
  2. Create DA_Enemy_SluiceKeeper with two phases: cone sweep then alternating water-lane area effects; all art/meshes/VFX are acquisition/authoring tasks.
  3. Place BP_DungeonController and encounter spawners; connect their state to the backend instance record and zone transfer system.
  4. Build WBP_DungeonFinder with party readiness, requirements, queue/reservation status and cancel. Start a simple explicit party-entry queue before automated role matching.
  5. Reopen party/quest/loot/recovery components to handle instance identity and reconnect; test wipe/reset after one already-rewarded encounter.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Elite phases, boss telegraphs and instanced dungeons. Rule owner: URPGDungeonInstanceComponent. This asset’s role is A small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.

  1. Party leader requests SluiceVault; backend validates roster/revision, requirements and available instance capacity and reserves a server.
  2. Each member receives their own identity-bound transfer ticket; one player failure does not cause whole-server travel of unrelated players.
  3. Instance initializes registered encounters and checkpoint. Boss health thresholds/time rules select phases and publish telegraph state before impact.
  4. Server validates all melee/projectile/area hits; telegraph graphics cannot cause damage, and low visual settings must retain gameplay-critical shape cues.
  5. Boss defeat creates a unique durable encounter/reward receipt and completion fact for quests; loot rights use the declared party eligibility snapshot.
  6. Reconnect returns to an active reserved instance when valid. Server crash recovers from durable checkpoint under a documented reset policy with existing reward entitlements preserved.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_SluiceVault / Boss_SluiceKeeper / Party_ABCD. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Party roster changes after reservation -> require refresh or explicit allowed member update; no unauthorized entrant.
Boss threshold processed twice -> one phase transition/cue sequence.
Server restart after boss reward -> no second loot/quest completion.
Player disconnects during telegraph -> server simulation continues; rejoin obeys safe checkpoint policy.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
